children: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA, Financials) is providing another signal to investors that demand has not hit its peak, the semiconductor company fueling much of the AI infrastructure development.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said Thursday he expects the company to sell twice as many chips in the next year as it did this year.
His rationale was straightforward. AI investment is spreading across industries, economies and countries. The prediction adds to numbers that Nvidia has already presented to investors.

Management said consumer expectations are pointing to another doubling of growth next year. Nvidia also projected around 70% revenue growth for the fiscal year ending January 2028, bringing revenue to almost $673 billion.
That forecast might not even capture the entire demand.
Management has classified the outlook as supply tight, implying Nvidia's capacity to ship chips could remain one of the largest impediments to growth.
Last year, Huang said the company shipped around 6 million Blackwell GPUs in four quarters. Now Rubin is coming up as the next big part of the product cycle.

That leaves investors with a different question than they had at the start of the AI boom. Nvidia no longer has to prove only demand. The next question is whether its supply chain can handle the huge volume that Huang now expects.

title: Jensen Huang just gave Nvidia investors a massive 2027 signal
